name: Provincial public-sector asset manager for multiple client institutions (pooled funds, cost recovery)
modelled_on: An Ontario public-sector investment manager that serves several public pension and insurance clients (name withheld), public information for 2019 to 2022
summary: This organisation is a provincial public-sector asset manager that invested about $79 billion at the end of 2021 for a handful of public bodies: a public service pension plan, a judges' pension plan, a jointly sponsored workplace pension trust and a workers' compensation insurance board with two funds. Each client keeps its own statement of investment policies and asset mix; the manager advises on that mix, then carries it out through pooled funds in which clients hold units and through segregated holdings, mainly private assets that were not yet pooled. It earns no profit: as a not-for-profit, non-share capital corporation it budgets its costs each year and recovers them from clients through cost allocation statements. Internal teams run public equities, fixed income, credit, total portfolio overlays and private market deals, but much of the money sits with about 120 external managers and private fund general partners, so manager selection and monitoring, capital calls and quarterly valuations are large workloads. About 240 staff in one Toronto office work in divisions for investments, client relations, investment risk, operations and technology, finance, and legal and compliance, plus human resources, communications, internal audit and an executive office with the board secretariat. It reports to each client separately every month and quarter, publishes an annual report to the Minister of Finance and the public, and is governed by a board partly appointed by the Minister and partly elected by its client members.

profile.ownership: Member-based, not-for-profit, non-share capital corporation created by the manager's governing act, 2015; members are its client institutions; operates on a cost recovery basis at arm's length from government

process_map.name: Respond to a prospective client's request for proposal
process_map.description: An eligible public body reviewing how its fund is managed sends a request for proposal or asks for a presentation. The client relationship team leads a response with portfolio construction, finance, legal and the CEO covering an illustrative asset mix, the pools available, the cost recovery approach and reporting. Sales cycles are long because prospects' boards decide slowly and some types of body need a regulation change before they can join.
process_map.unit_of_work: one proposal to a prospective client

evidence.note: Eligible members defined at launch (2017); the model manager expected a long sales cycle (2018) and four public bodies selected it after competitive evaluations and RFPs (2023); volume is a tier C estimate.

process_map.name: Onboard a new client and transition its assets
process_map.description: After a client signs an investment management agreement, a cross-functional team maps its investment policy to the model manager's pools and strategies, opens custody and client accounts, sets up reporting, cost allocation and compliance rules, and moves the legacy portfolio. Legacy managers are kept, terminated or transitioned and assets move into pools in kind where possible. The hard parts are timing the transfer around market risk, legacy private holdings that cannot move, and agreeing day-one positions and values with the old custodian.

evidence.note: Founding clients transferred in July 2017; two clients joined in 2020 (judges' plan with $420 million and WISE Trust); new clients onboard after regulatory changes and contracts; frequency tier C.

process_map.name: Review a client's investment policy and asset mix
process_map.description: Each client keeps its own asset mix and approves its own statement of investment policies. At least once a year, and in a fuller asset-liability study about every four years, the portfolio construction team works with the client's staff, actuary and board to test the current mix against liabilities, capital market assumptions and stress scenarios, and recommends a strategic asset allocation with ranges. Once the client's board approves, the new targets, ranges, benchmarks and restrictions are loaded into rebalancing, risk, compliance and performance.
process_map.unit_of_work: one client portfolio's policy and asset mix review

evidence.note: Clients keep asset mix control and approve their SIPP; the insurance client reviews its SIPP yearly with an asset-liability study at least every four years; the model manager advises.

process_map.name: Take in client contribution and withdrawal instructions
process_map.description: Clients send instructions when they have cash to invest, such as pension contributions or insurance premiums, or need cash to pay pensions and benefits. Client service checks the instruction against authorised signers and a call-back list, confirms amount and value date, and turns it into pool subscriptions or redemptions and segregated account cash moves that follow the client's current asset mix and liquidity plan. Late or changed instructions and large same-day withdrawals cause most of the rework.

evidence.note: No public description of the model manager's instruction handling; based on the common practice of multi-client pooled fund managers.

process_map.name: Handle client service and information requests
process_map.description: Clients ask for holdings for their financial statements, data for actuarial valuations, analysis for a board meeting, explanations of returns or costs, and answers for their regulators. Client service logs each request, routes analysis to performance, risk or finance, reviews the answer and sends it within the agreed service level. Requests cluster around client board cycles and year end.

evidence.note: The model manager describes responsive client teams and hands-on support; volume tier C.

process_map.name: Produce monthly client reports
process_map.description: Each month, after pools and portfolios are closed and performance is approved, client reporting builds a package for each client portfolio: market values by pool and asset class, units held, returns against benchmarks, asset mix against policy ranges, cash flows, rebalancing done and compliance with the client's investment policy. Analysts reconcile figures across accounting, performance and risk sources, the manager reviews and the relationship manager releases it. Late private market values and performance restatements are the usual causes of delay.

evidence.note: The model manager reports regularly on performance and risk and describes timely reporting; monthly frequency is common practice (tier C).

process_map.name: Report quarterly to each client's board
process_map.description: Each quarter the model manager prepares a fuller report and presentation for each client's investment committee or board: total fund and asset class performance including private markets on quarter-end values, risk and stress tests, liquidity, compliance, costs charged, stewardship and outlook. Relationship managers, portfolio construction and risk staff present it at the client's meeting and log follow-up questions. The lag on private valuations means the report goes out six to ten weeks after quarter end.
process_map.unit_of_work: one client portfolio's quarterly report and presentation

evidence.note: The insurance client reviews fund performance, risk and compliance at least quarterly; the pension client monitors the model manager; content and timing tier C.

process_map.name: Support clients' year-end audits
process_map.description: At year end each client's auditor needs confirmed holdings, unit balances, values and income for the client's financial statements. Fund accounting prepares confirmation letters and schedules, answers questions on private market valuations and provides the pools' audited statements once signed. Timing is tight because most clients close on 31 December and need figures in the same weeks.
process_map.unit_of_work: one client portfolio's year-end audit package

evidence.note: Common practice for a manager of client portfolios; one package per portfolio a year.

process_map.name: Set capital market assumptions
process_map.description: Once a year the portfolio construction and research team updates long-term expected returns, volatilities and correlations for each asset class and risk factor from economic research and market data, and publishes a house view. The CIO challenges and approves them, and they drive asset mix advice for every client, the investment plan and the strategic plan. Changes must be explained to clients whose recommended mix shifts.

evidence.note: The model manager describes long-term return and risk forecasts feeding asset-liability studies and publishes a World View.

process_map.name: Rebalance client portfolios to their asset mix
process_map.description: Market moves, cash flows and private market calls and distributions pull each client portfolio away from its approved asset mix. The total portfolio team checks every client's weights against targets and ranges, nets client flows where it can, and decides how to rebalance: switching units between pools, adjusting segregated holdings, or using futures and currency overlays when private assets cannot be traded. Each client's mix is different, so one market move creates several separate rebalancing decisions.

evidence.note: The model manager rebalanced into equities and credit in 2020 and cites systematic rebalancing in 2022; the insurance client policy allows derivatives for rebalancing and remapping private over and underweights.

process_map.name: Forecast liquidity for each client portfolio
process_map.description: Each week the total portfolio team rolls forward a cash and liquidity forecast for every client portfolio and pool: expected client flows, capital calls on unfunded commitments, distributions, margin and settlement needs. It tests whether liquid assets cover stressed outflows and flags any client at risk of becoming a forced seller. The forecast depends on uncertain call timing from general partners and on clients warning the model manager early about large payments.
process_map.unit_of_work: one weekly liquidity forecast across all portfolios

evidence.note: The model manager manages liquidity to avoid forced selling; the insurance client monitors liquidity coverage at least monthly; weekly cadence tier C.

process_map.name: Manage derivative overlays, currency hedges and leverage
process_map.description: The total portfolio team uses futures, currency forwards and swaps to rebalance quickly, hedge foreign currency to each client's policy and, from 2022, apply leverage at the total portfolio level. It sizes each client's overlay, checks counterparty and margin capacity and sends orders to the trading desk. Rolling contracts and keeping overlays in line with changing client weights is steady daily work.

evidence.note: Dynamic foreign exchange and active asset allocation (2021); leverage at total portfolio level (2022); volume tier C.

process_map.name: Set the annual investment plan and strategy benchmarks
process_map.description: Each year every asset class team writes a plan: target size, pacing of private commitments, internal versus external split, manager changes, new pools and the benchmark and risk budget for each strategy. The CIO, risk and finance check the plans against capital market assumptions, clients' asset mixes and the cost budget, and the board approves the consolidated plan. Benchmarks set here drive performance measurement and incentive pay, so changes are contested.

evidence.note: The insurance client says the model manager establishes benchmarks and relative risk targets for each strategy; the model manager adopted a five-year strategic plan in 2022.

process_map.name: Launch a new investment pool
process_map.description: When the model manager decides to pool an asset class, a project team designs the pool's legal form, guidelines, unit classes and valuation policy, drafts trust and subscription documents with outside counsel, opens custody accounts, registers for tax and configures systems. On launch day clients' existing holdings move into the pool in kind at agreed values in exchange for units, and every client's records must agree. Public equity pools launched in 2020 and 2021, a public market alternatives pool in 2021 and the first private market pool, infrastructure, in 2022.

evidence.note: Five pools launched from November 2020 to 2022 (about 0.14 a month); the model manager cited work on pool architecture, governance and legal frameworks.

process_map.name: Calculate and approve pool unit prices
process_map.description: For each pool and valuation date the custodian produces a net asset value from priced holdings, accruals and expenses, and the model manager's unit pricing team checks it: price moves against tolerances, stale or missing prices, accruals, cost recovery charges, private holding values and units outstanding from the register. The approved net asset value divided by units in issue gives the unit price used for subscriptions, redemptions and client values. A wrong price affects every client in the pool and must be corrected and compensated, so checks are strict.
process_map.unit_of_work: one pool unit price for one valuation date

evidence.note: Pool count from the model manager; daily public market pricing by the custodian with the model manager review is common practice, not stated by the model manager; unit pricing errors are a recognised risk (ASIC and APRA guide).

process_map.name: Process pool subscriptions, redemptions and switches
process_map.description: The transfer agency team processes each subscription, redemption and switch between pools: it checks the instruction is authorised and before the dealing cut-off, applies the unit price for the dealing date, issues or cancels units in the unitholder register, instructs the cash or in-kind transfer between client and pool accounts, and confirms units and values to the client. Pools have few but very large unitholders, so one error can move hundreds of millions of dollars between clients.

evidence.note: Clients hold units of the model manager pools; the in-house transfer agency process is assumed from common practice.

process_map.name: Invest or raise pool cash across mandates
process_map.description: When net subscriptions or redemptions hit a pool, its portfolio managers invest or raise the cash across the pool's internal strategies and external manager mandates so the pool stays at its target allocations and within its guidelines. They decide which mandates to fund or draw from, send orders for internal sleeves and cash notices to external managers. Large same-day redemptions from several clients make this harder.
process_map.unit_of_work: one pool cash deployment or raise

evidence.note: Common practice for multi-manager pools; volume from four pools with three to five flow events a month each.

process_map.name: Allocate pool income and file pool tax returns
process_map.description: Each pool is assumed to be a trust for tax purposes, so its net income and realised gains are allocated to unitholders each year and reported to them and the Canada Revenue Agency. The tax team computes taxable income by pool, allocates it to each client by units held through the year, prepares the trust return and slips and documents treaty positions. Clients are tax-exempt public bodies, but the filings are still required and must agree with audited statements.

evidence.note: Legal form of the pools not confirmed in sources opened; trust treatment is common for Canadian pooled funds.

process_map.name: Make internal public equity investment decisions
process_map.description: Internal portfolio managers run factor, index, fundamental and portfolio completion strategies inside the public equity pools. They review models, research and limits, decide trades and enter orders in the order management system, where pre-trade compliance checks guidelines. Order volume rises at month end, at index changes and when pools receive flows.

evidence.note: The model manager describes internal factor and fundamental equity strategies; about two thirds of internal orders assumed to be equity (tier C).

process_map.name: Make internal fixed income and public credit decisions
process_map.description: Fixed income and global credit portfolio managers run government bond, money market and public credit portfolios used for liability matching, liquidity and return. They set duration and curve positions against each portfolio's benchmark, pick bonds and loans, and send orders to the desk, often as request-for-quote trades with dealers. Liquidity needs from client withdrawals and capital calls are met first from these portfolios.
process_map.unit_of_work: one fixed income or credit order

evidence.note: Fixed income $17.2 billion and global credit $6.0 billion at end 2021 with internal credit decisions; about one third of internal orders assumed (tier C).

process_map.name: Execute public market trades
process_map.description: Traders work orders from internal portfolio managers, pool rebalancing and the total portfolio overlay through approved brokers and dealer platforms, choosing between program, block, request-for-quote and algorithmic execution. They record fills and allocate executions across pools and client accounts in the order management system. Best execution reviews and counterparty limits constrain which brokers can be used.

evidence.note: An internal desk is assumed once strategies were internalised; not described in sources opened.

process_map.name: Capture and confirm trades
process_map.description: Trade support checks every executed trade against the broker's confirmation in the matching service: security, quantity, price, commission, settlement date and settlement instructions. Unmatched or wrong trades are queried with the trader and broker, and matched trades are released to the custodian. Derivative trades are also confirmed and passed to collateral management and every trade feeds post-trade compliance.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume from orders split across pools and client accounts.

process_map.name: Settle trades and resolve failed settlements
process_map.description: The custodian settles each instructed trade in the market. Trade support monitors pending and failed settlements across internal accounts and external manager accounts, chases brokers and the custodian to fix mismatches, claims compensation for late settlement and tells cash management about expected cash. Fails cluster in emerging markets and around wrong settlement instructions.

evidence.note: Common practice; emerging markets pool from 2021 raises fail rates.

process_map.name: Process corporate actions
process_map.description: The custodian sends notices of dividends, splits, mergers, rights issues and tender offers on internally held securities. The analyst checks terms against a second source, asks the portfolio manager for elections on voluntary events, instructs the custodian before the deadline and checks entitlements are booked. Missed voluntary deadlines are costly and must be compensated.

evidence.note: Based on 2,000 to 4,000 internally held securities; tier C.

process_map.name: Vote proxies and engage with companies
process_map.description: The model manager votes the shares it holds for clients at company meetings under its voting guidelines. The responsible investing team receives ballots and research through a proxy advisor platform, reviews contentious items such as director elections, pay and climate proposals, records votes and engages selected companies. Voting peaks from April to June and results feed client and public stewardship reporting.

evidence.note: 4,177 meetings in 58 markets voted in 2020, about 348 a month; seasonal range tier C.

process_map.name: Reconcile positions and cash daily
process_map.description: Every business day the reconciliations team compares the model manager's book of record with the custodian, external managers and brokers and counterparties for positions, cash and derivatives across all pool, client and mandate accounts. A reconciliation tool matches most items automatically and analysts investigate breaks, assign them to trade support, cash or data teams and age them until resolved. Clean positions are released to pricing, risk, performance and accounting, so breaks delay everything downstream.
process_map.unit_of_work: one business day's reconciliation across all accounts

evidence.note: Common practice; account count grows with 124 external mandates (2020) and four pools (2021).

process_map.name: Manage daily cash and funding
process_map.description: Each morning the cash team projects cash in every pool, client and mandate account from settlements, unit transactions, capital calls, distributions, fees and client flows, then funds shortfalls, sweeps surpluses into money market holdings and books foreign exchange for settlements. Wires above set thresholds need two approvers and a call-back on new payment details. Late capital call notices and same-day client requests cause most exceptions.

evidence.note: Common practice; not described in sources opened.

process_map.name: Manage derivative margin and collateral
process_map.description: For futures, forwards and swaps the collateral team agrees daily margin calls with clearing brokers and counterparties, checks exposure calculations, chooses eligible collateral, instructs movements and resolves disputes. Margin needs rise sharply in volatile markets and feed the liquidity forecast and counterparty exposure monitoring.

evidence.note: Common practice; about three calls a day across overlay and credit derivatives.

process_map.name: Onboard a broker or derivative counterparty
process_map.description: Before trading with a new broker or derivative counterparty, the model manager completes due diligence, credit approval by risk, legal agreements such as ISDA master agreements with collateral terms, and set-up of settlement instructions and connectivity. The approved counterparty is added to the order management system with limits. Negotiating collateral terms can take months.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate for a firm building internal trading.

process_map.name: Search for and select an external manager
process_map.description: When the investment plan calls for a new or replacement mandate, the manager research team screens candidates, sends due diligence questionnaires, meets shortlisted firms and runs investment and operational due diligence on process, people, track record, fees and controls. The asset class team writes a recommendation, risk gives an independent view and the investment committee approves. A search typically takes three to six months and fees and terms are negotiated before onboarding.

evidence.note: Roster rebuilt from 200 to 124 managers in 2020 with new strategic partnerships; over $2 billion committed to new credit managers in 2022; duration tier C.

process_map.name: Onboard an external manager
process_map.description: Once a manager is approved, legal finalises the management agreement and guidelines, operations opens the custody account, sets up data feeds, settlement instructions and reconciliation, compliance codes the guidelines into monitoring rules and finance loads the fee schedule. The account is then funded from the pool or client account. Gaps between the legal guidelines and the coded rules are a common source of later breaches.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume follows manager hires.

process_map.name: Monitor external managers
process_map.description: Each month the manager research team and asset class portfolio managers review every external mandate's returns against benchmark, risk, positioning, guideline compliance and organisational changes, with deeper quarterly meetings and an annual operational due diligence refresh. Managers that underperform or lose key staff go on a watch list and the team recommends keeping, resizing or terminating. With over one hundred mandates, keeping reviews current is a constant load.
process_map.unit_of_work: one monthly review of one external mandate

evidence.note: 124 external managers at end 2020; review depth tier C.

process_map.name: Terminate a manager and transition its assets
process_map.description: When a mandate is terminated or a new client's legacy managers are replaced, the team plans the transition: notice to the manager, choice between in-kind transfer, liquidation or a transition manager, a cost estimate and reallocation to target mandates or internal strategies. Operations closes the account after final fees and residual cash are settled. The model manager cut its roster from 200 to 124 managers in 2020, so transitions were frequent in the period.

evidence.note: 76 terminations in 2020 (about six a month) with one-time transition costs; later years fewer (tier C).

process_map.name: Validate and pay external manager fees
process_map.description: External managers invoice management and performance fees, usually quarterly. Fund accounting recalculates each fee from the agreed schedule, average assets from the custodian and any performance hurdle, resolves differences with the manager, gets approval and instructs payment from the right pool or client account. Validated fees feed cost reporting because external fees are a large part of what clients pay.

evidence.note: About 124 mandates invoicing quarterly gives about 40 a month.

process_map.name: Screen and diligence private equity co-investments
process_map.description: The private equity team receives co-investment offers from its fund partners, usually with short deadlines and no fee or carry. It screens each against the investment plan, then for promising deals reviews the sponsor's diligence, adds its own work with outside advisers on the business, valuation, financing and ESG risks, models returns and writes an investment memo. In 2021 the team closed seven direct and co-investments totalling $800 million.
process_map.unit_of_work: one co-investment taken into due diligence

evidence.note: Seven private equity direct and co-investments in 2021; co-investments alongside general partners on no fee, no carry terms; screening ratio tier C.

process_map.name: Screen and diligence infrastructure and real estate direct investments
process_map.description: Infrastructure and real estate teams source direct, joint venture and partnered deals such as take-privates, full acquisitions and development projects with operating partners. They screen fit, then run technical, market, regulatory, legal, tax and environmental due diligence with outside advisers, build long-term cash flow models and write an investment memo. Large deals are bid in auctions with partners, so work is lost when bids fail.
process_map.unit_of_work: one direct real asset opportunity taken into due diligence

evidence.note: 2021 deals included a 100% infrastructure acquisition, a take-private with a partner, a life sciences development and a 12-project industrial joint venture; screening volume tier C.

process_map.name: Underwrite private credit investments
process_map.description: The global credit team underwrites direct lending co-investments, loan participations and separately managed private credit accounts with strategic partners. It reviews the borrower, structure, covenants and collateral, compares terms with public credit, sizes the position for the single global credit portfolio and writes a credit memo. After funding it monitors covenants and amendments through the partner.
process_map.unit_of_work: one private credit opportunity taken into due diligence

evidence.note: Direct lending investment with a partner (2021), a co-investment alongside a partner (2020) and internal direct credit decisions; volume tier C.

process_map.name: Approve investments at the investment committee
process_map.description: The internal investment committee, chaired by the CIO with the CEO and chief risk officer, reviews memos for direct investments, fund commitments, new external mandates, follow-ons and exits above team authority. The investment office circulates papers, records decisions and conditions and tracks delegated limits; deals above the CEO's authority go to the board. Committee dates set the pace for deal teams facing seller deadlines.

evidence.note: Committee membership and delegated limits are common practice; not stated in sources opened.

process_map.name: Make a private fund commitment
process_map.description: Teams commit to private equity, infrastructure, real estate and private credit funds run by general partners; in 2021 private equity alone made four new commitments totalling $1.5 billion. The work covers reviewing the offering memorandum and data room, reference calls, operational due diligence, fee and term analysis, an investment memo, negotiating the partnership agreement and side letter, and deciding which pool or client accounts take the commitment. Most private assets sat in segregated client accounts in the period, so each commitment is split among the clients whose asset mix needs it.

evidence.note: Fund commitments named in 2020 and 2021 releases; split across client accounts is tier C.

process_map.name: Close and fund private investments
process_map.description: After approval, legal and the deal team finalise and sign the purchase, co-investment or subscription documents, and private markets operations sets up the commitment or holding, allocates it across pools or client accounts and funds the closing. Announcements go to communications. Closings often move at short notice, which strains same-day funding and approvals.
process_map.unit_of_work: one closing (direct deal or fund commitment)

evidence.note: Common practice; volume from about 35 direct deals and 15 fund commitments a year.

process_map.name: Process capital calls
process_map.description: General partners send capital call notices, usually with about ten business days' notice, stating amount, purpose and due date. Private markets operations checks each notice against the commitment, unfunded balance and partnership terms, splits it across the pools or client accounts that own the interest, records it, arranges funding and confirms payment. Notices arrive by email and portals in many formats, so validation and keying are manual.

evidence.note: ILPA's template exists to standardise capital call notices for limited partners; notice period and volume tier C.

process_map.name: Process distributions from private investments
process_map.description: Funds and direct holdings return cash as income, realised gains and return of capital, some of which can be recalled. The team matches each notice to cash received at the custodian, splits it across owning accounts, classifies it for accounting and tax and updates remaining commitments. Unannounced or poorly described distributions are the main exceptions.

evidence.note: ILPA template covers distribution notices; volume tier C.

process_map.name: Value private investments each quarter
process_map.description: Each quarter the valuations team values every private holding: fund interests from general partners' capital account statements, rolled forward for calls, distributions and market moves when statements arrive late, and direct investments and properties from independent appraisals or internal models checked against valuation policy. A valuation committee approves the set, which updates pool unit prices, client portfolio values and performance. Statements arrive 45 to 90 days after quarter end, so values are revised after first reporting.
process_map.unit_of_work: one private holding valued for a quarter

evidence.note: The insurance client policy requires non-traded assets valued at least annually and reviewed quarterly, with the model manager reviewing third-party valuations; IPEV guidelines set fair value practice; holding count tier C.

process_map.name: Monitor direct private holdings
process_map.description: Deal teams monitor direct and co-investments and real estate held with operating partners: they review quarterly results and budgets, attend boards where the model manager has a seat, approve major decisions such as refinancing or capital spending and flag problems. Monitoring reports inform valuations and exit decisions.
process_map.unit_of_work: one quarterly review of one direct holding

evidence.note: Active asset management of direct real estate and a fully owned infrastructure business; count tier C.

process_map.name: Sell a private investment
process_map.description: When a holding meets its plan or no longer fits, the team prepares a sale: picks advisers, runs a sale process or negotiates with partners, gets committee approval and closes, with operations booking proceeds across owning accounts. In 2020 the model manager sold 12 properties worth about $648 million.

evidence.note: 12 property disposals in 2020, about one a month; other years tier C.

process_map.name: Subscribe to and redeem from hedge funds
process_map.description: The public market alternatives pool holds hedge funds and alternative funds that deal monthly or quarterly with notice periods and possible gates. When the pool needs to add or raise cash, the team decides which funds to use, sends subscription or redemption forms before the notice deadline, and tracks acknowledgements and settlement, which for redemptions can come weeks after the dealing date with a holdback until the fund's audit. Notice periods make this the slowest source of liquidity in the pools.

evidence.note: Public Market Alternatives Pool launched 2021; dealing terms are common hedge fund practice, not stated by the model manager.

process_map.name: Run data warehouse loads and reporting data sets
process_map.description: Each night the data engineering team runs loads from the book of record, custodian files, the private markets system and performance results into the investment data warehouse, checks completeness and data quality rules, fixes failed jobs and publishes the data sets used for client reports, risk reports and ad hoc client requests. A failed load holds up the morning's reporting.

evidence.note: Data engineering team on the current org chart and a client reporting framework since 2018; nightly batch design is common practice (tier C).

process_map.name: Measure risk and monitor limits daily
process_map.description: Each day the risk team loads reconciled positions, prices and benchmarks into the risk system, calculates active risk, value at risk, factor and currency exposures, leverage and liquidity for every pool and client portfolio, and checks them against board limits and each client's policy ranges. Breaches and near breaches go to the CIO and portfolio managers with a required action and date. Private assets are represented by public proxies, a known weakness.

evidence.note: A dedicated risk team monitors portfolios daily against target allocations and risk tolerances; a risk system was in place in 2018.

process_map.name: Review new investments and mandates for risk
process_map.description: Before the investment committee decides on a direct investment, fund commitment or new mandate, the investment risk team reviews the memo independently: concentration, leverage, liquidity, currency, fit with risk budgets, key person and counterparty risk and stress scenarios. Its written opinion goes into the committee paper. Tight deal timelines often leave little time for the review.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian pension investment managers; volume equals committee submissions.

process_map.name: Report risk and run stress tests
process_map.description: Monthly the risk team produces risk reports for each client portfolio and the CIO, and quarterly for the board and client boards: exposures, active risk use, limit status, liquidity coverage, counterparty exposure and stress tests such as an inflation shock or equity crash. Analysts check the numbers, write commentary and answer client questions. Each client wants its own format, which multiplies the work.

evidence.note: The model manager uses stress tests such as higher inflation; the insurance client reviews risk and compliance at least quarterly.

process_map.name: Monitor counterparty exposure
process_map.description: Weekly, and daily in stressed markets, the investment risk team measures exposure to each derivative counterparty, broker and the custodian net of collateral, compares it with credit limits and recommends limit cuts or extra collateral. Results feed the monthly risk report.

evidence.note: Common practice once derivatives and leverage are used.

process_map.name: Manage enterprise and operational risk
process_map.description: The enterprise risk team keeps the risk register, runs quarterly risk and control self-assessments with each department, logs operational incidents such as unit pricing or payment errors, tracks fixes, tests business continuity plans and reports to the board. In 2020 the business continuity program moved all staff to remote work.

evidence.note: Business continuity program supported remote work in 2020; volume tier C.

process_map.name: Monitor investment compliance
process_map.description: Compliance codes each pool's, mandate's and client's investment restrictions into the compliance engine, reviews pre-trade warnings and runs post-trade checks daily on all holdings, including external managers' accounts. Analysts investigate each alert, confirm whether it is a real breach, agree a fix with the portfolio manager or external manager and report breaches to clients and the board. False alerts from bad reference data take much of the time.
process_map.unit_of_work: one business day's compliance run with its alerts

evidence.note: The model manager must comply with each client's SIP&P; monitoring design is common practice.

process_map.name: Run code of conduct, personal trading and attestations
process_map.description: Employees pre-clear personal trades, report holdings, gifts and outside activities, and once a year attest that they followed the code of conduct and conflict of interest policy. Compliance checks each request against restricted lists of companies the model manager is dealing in, follows up late attestations and reports results to the audit committee.

evidence.note: Common practice for investment managers; volume from about 240 staff.

process_map.name: Make regulatory and statistical filings
process_map.description: Compliance and legal prepare filings that arise from the model manager's holdings and status: ownership reports when holdings cross thresholds, foreign investment and competition filings for direct deals and statistical surveys. Each filing has a fixed deadline and needs data from operations.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Measure performance and attribution
process_map.description: After month end the performance team calculates time-weighted returns net of costs for every client portfolio, pool, asset class, strategy and external mandate, compares them with benchmarks and explains the difference through allocation and selection attribution. Private assets are updated when quarterly values arrive, which restates earlier months. Results are reconciled to accounting, approved and released to client reporting, investment teams and the board.
process_map.unit_of_work: one monthly performance cycle for one client portfolio or pool

evidence.note: The model manager reports net returns by client and asset class against benchmarks; GIPS asset owner standards call for net-of-fee time-weighted returns; five portfolios and four pools a month.

process_map.name: Maintain security, price and reference data
process_map.description: The investment data team maintains the security master, prices, benchmark constituents and returns, exchange rates and account structures that every downstream process uses. It validates daily vendor prices against tolerances, chases missing or stale prices, sets up new securities and accounts and manages feed changes with technology.
process_map.unit_of_work: one business day's data validation cycle

evidence.note: Common practice; not described in sources opened.

process_map.name: Close the books for pools and client portfolios
process_map.description: Each month fund accounting closes the books for every pool and client portfolio: it reviews the custodian's accounting against the model manager's book of record, books private market capital activity, accruals, manager fees and cost recovery charges, checks the unitholder register against pool net assets and signs off net asset values. The approved package feeds performance, client reporting, cost allocation and the annual audit. Late private market information and manual journals slow the close.
process_map.unit_of_work: one monthly close for one pool or client portfolio

evidence.note: Common practice; an model manager posting names an Investment Operations and Accounting group; five portfolios and four pools.

process_map.name: Prepare and audit annual financial statements
process_map.description: After 31 December, financial reporting prepares audited statements for the model manager itself and for each pool, with notes on fair value, related parties and cost recovery. The external auditor tests controls, confirms holdings and challenges private market valuations, and the audit committee approves the statements before they go to clients and into the annual report.
process_map.unit_of_work: one set of audited annual statements

evidence.note: The model manager publishes annual reports with financial statements; pool statements assumed; the model manager plus four pools gives five sets a year.

process_map.name: Prepare the annual cost budget
process_map.description: Each autumn finance builds the model manager's operating budget for the next year: salaries and incentives for planned headcount, technology and data, premises, professional fees and expected external manager fees, with a forecast of each client's share. Department heads submit requests, the executives cut them to the cost target, clients are consulted because they pay, and the board approves. Because all costs are recovered from clients, budget growth is watched against the savings the model manager promised.

evidence.note: Cost recovery basis and reported savings of $10 million (2020) and $20 million (2021); budget mechanics tier C.

process_map.name: Allocate costs to clients and bill them
process_map.description: The model manager charges clients only what it costs to run. Finance allocates actual operating costs each month to client portfolios and pools with agreed keys such as assets by strategy and activity measures, adds directly attributable external manager and transaction costs, accrues the charges and each quarter issues every client a cost allocation statement and invoice, with a year-end true-up to audited costs. Clients' finance staff review the allocations closely, so the keys and any changes must be documented and explained.
process_map.unit_of_work: one client portfolio's quarterly cost allocation statement

evidence.note: Cost recovery only, no profit, and members do not assume each other's liabilities; peers' costs are benchmarked by CEM; allocation keys and quarterly invoicing are tier C.

process_map.name: Pay corporate vendor invoices
process_map.description: The accounts payable clerk receives invoices for data, technology, legal, audit, premises and other corporate costs, matches them to contracts or purchase orders, routes them for approval under the delegation of authority and pays them in weekly runs. Paid costs post to the general ledger and feed monthly cost allocation to clients.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: File tax returns and recover withholding tax
process_map.description: The tax team files returns and keeps tax status documents for the model manager and the pools in Canada and abroad, recovers foreign withholding tax on dividends and interest through relief at source or reclaims, and reviews the tax structure of private investments. Reclaims take months to years and must be tracked market by market.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Procure and onboard a vendor
process_map.description: When a department needs a new service, such as a data feed, platform, adviser or consultant, procurement runs a competitive or justified single-source process, checks the vendor's financial, security and privacy controls with technology, negotiates the contract with legal and sets the vendor up for payment. Public sector expectations mean competitive bid thresholds are applied strictly.

evidence.note: Common practice for a public sector body; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Manage IT changes and releases
process_map.description: Changes to investment and corporate systems, such as set-up for a new pool, a new data feed, a vendor upgrade or a report change, are raised as change requests, assessed for risk, tested by business users, approved at a weekly change board and released in set windows. Emergency fixes follow a shorter path and are reviewed afterwards.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Run the IT service desk and access management
process_map.description: The service desk handles incidents and requests from staff, including device set-up, software access and password resets, and provisions access to investment systems on approved requests. Each quarter system owners recertify who has access and security reviews privileged accounts. Joiners, movers and leavers drive much of the volume in a growing firm.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Deliver technology projects
process_map.description: Multi-year programs replaced and upgraded front, middle and back office systems as the model manager built its own operations. Each project, such as pool accounting set-up, a private markets system or the data warehouse, passes stage gates for business case, vendor selection, design, build, testing and go-live, with business analysts working beside operations and investment users.
process_map.unit_of_work: one project stage gate or release

evidence.note: Multi-year programs to upgrade processes, systems and teams (2020); software as a service with no legacy systems (2018); volume tier C.

process_map.name: Negotiate investment legal agreements
process_map.description: Legal counsel negotiate the agreements behind every investment and mandate: limited partnership agreements and side letters, co-investment and shareholder agreements, external manager agreements, ISDA and collateral agreements and client agreements, using outside law firms on large deals. They track key terms such as fees, most favoured nation rights and consents in the document system.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume from deals, fund commitments, manager hires and counterparties.

process_map.name: Run internal audit engagements
process_map.description: Internal audit builds a risk-based annual plan approved by the audit committee and runs about eight to ten engagements a year, for example on unit pricing, capital call payments, cost allocation or access controls. Each engagement covers planning, walkthroughs, control testing, a draft report agreed with management and tracking of actions until closed.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Recruit and onboard staff
process_map.description: Hiring managers open a requisition against the approved budget, HR posts the role and works with search firms, coordinates interviews and assessments, makes an offer within the pay band and runs background checks. Onboarding then sets up payroll, system access and code of conduct training. The model manager grew from about 100 staff in 2018 toward a planned 250 to 300, so hiring was a steady load.

evidence.note: Growth from about 100 (2018) to 406 (2026); volume tier C.

process_map.name: Run performance reviews and incentive pay
process_map.description: Employees have reviews every six months, and once a year managers rate performance and propose incentive awards that depend partly on investment results against benchmarks. HR calibrates ratings and models incentive pools against the budget, the board's human resources committee approves executive pay, and approved awards go to payroll.

evidence.note: Reviews every six months (employer review); executive incentive pay disclosed in the 2022 annual report.

process_map.name: Run payroll and benefits
process_map.description: HR operations runs payroll through an outsourced provider, enters joiners, leavers and pay changes, administers group benefits and enrolment in the defined benefit pension plan, and reconciles payroll to the general ledger. Payroll is the largest part of the operating budget and flows into cost allocation.

evidence.note: Defined benefit pension and group benefits from employer review; two runs a month tier C.

process_map.name: Publish the annual report and results
process_map.description: Each spring the model manager publishes its annual report and a results release with the weighted average client return, asset class results, assets under management, transactions, cost savings and audited statements, and from 2022 a separate responsible investing report. Communications coordinates writers across investments, finance and risk, the board approves, and the report goes to the Minister of Finance, clients and the public.

evidence.note: Annual reports and results releases published each April for 2017 onward.

process_map.name: Handle media and stakeholder relations
process_map.description: Communications answers media questions, announces transactions and appointments, maintains the website and prepares executives for interviews and conferences. Every deal announcement is cleared with partners and legal before release.

evidence.note: Releases carry a corporate communications contact; volume tier C.

process_map.name: Prepare and run board and committee meetings
process_map.description: The board of seven to eleven directors and its committees, typically audit, investment, risk, human resources and governance, meet on a quarterly cycle plus special meetings for large investments. The secretariat sets agendas with the chair and CEO, collects and checks management papers, publishes them on the board portal, records minutes and decisions and tracks actions. Paper deadlines create a monthly crunch for management.

evidence.note: Board of 7 to 11 directors; committee list and meeting count tier C.

process_map.name: Set the strategic and business plan
process_map.description: The CEO's office leads the multi-year strategic plan and the annual business plan: client growth, investment capability build, internal versus external management, technology and people priorities and cost targets. Executives draft initiatives, the board approves and the strategy team tracks progress quarterly. A five-year plan for 2023 to 2027 was approved in 2022.

evidence.note: Five-year strategic plan for 2023 to 2027 reported in the 2022 results.

process_map.name: Hold the members' meeting and director elections
process_map.description: The model manager is a member-based corporation whose members are its clients. Each year the secretariat runs the members' meeting, collects nominations from members, such as the two individuals the pension client may designate, and records the election of the six to eight member-elected directors who sit beside up to three directors appointed by the Minister of Finance.

evidence.note: Six to eight member-elected and one to three ministerial directors; the pension client designates two nominees.

process_map.name: Report to and work with the Ministry of Finance
process_map.description: The model manager operates at arm's length from government but sends its annual report to the Minister of Finance and works with the Ministry on regulations, for example when a regulation change is needed before a new type of public body can become a client, and on ministerial board appointments. The CEO's office coordinates these exchanges with legal.

evidence.note: Arm's length from government; ministerial appointments; onboarding of new clients after required regulatory changes.

assumptions: The snapshot is the end of 2021, inside the 2019 to 2022 reference period: about $79 billion, four client institutions with five portfolios, four pools and about 124 external managers. In 2019 there were only three portfolios and no pools; the file shows the 2021 state with ranges covering 2020 to 2022.

The model manager's annual report PDFs for 2019 to 2022 could not be read with the tools available, so numbers come from the model manager news releases, the model manager web pages, client web pages and secondary coverage. Headcount by unit, role costs and most volumes are tier C estimates. Later correction: the workflow authors did read the 2020 to 2022 annual reports (sources mgr_ar20, mgr_ar21, mgr_ar22). Numbers in this file have not yet been re-checked against them, apart from the cost recovery figure.

Total headcount of 242 is interpolated between about 100 staff in late 2018 and 406 full-time employees in 2026; the split between units follows common practice at Canadian public pension investment managers (investments about 37%, operations and technology about 28%).

Executive structure for 2021 is assumed: CEO, CIO, CFO, chief risk officer, chief client officer, general counsel and corporate secretary, and a chief operating officer over investment operations and technology. The model manager's current site lists a chief corporate officer and a chief technology and data officer instead of a COO; individual names are not used.

Loaded cost per hour: Job Bank Toronto wages (reference period 2023-2024) deflated 9% to 2021, plus variable pay (10% for analysts, 15% for managers), times a loading factor of 1.35 for benefits including the defined benefit pension, payroll taxes and overhead, over 1,950 paid hours a year. Investment professionals and executives are priced from estimated total pay because Job Bank medians omit their incentives; the CEO, CIO and chief risk officer use 2022 pay reported from the annual report with a 1.1 loading.

In 2021 only public equity and public market alternative assets were pooled; fixed income, real estate, private equity, infrastructure (pooled in 2022) and credit were held in segregated client accounts managed by the model manager. Private commitments are therefore split across client accounts, and client rebalancing mixes unit switches with segregated trades and overlays.

Pool unit prices are assumed to be calculated daily by the custodian and approved by the model manager, with unit transactions dealt on business days; the transfer agency register is assumed to be kept in-house on custodian records with controlled spreadsheets. The model manager has not published its pricing arrangements.
A single global custodian and fund accounting provider is assumed; its name is not sourced.

The Ontario Securities Commission is listed as a regulator because the pools and trading fall under Ontario securities law; its order concerning the model manager could not be opened, so no detail from it is used. Later correction: the workflow authors opened the order of 17 May 2017 (source osc_mgr_2017); it limits pool units to members who are accredited investors.
Costs are assumed to be allocated monthly with agreed keys and invoiced quarterly with a year-end true-up; the model manager states cost recovery but not its allocation method.

Clients are grouped into two external party types (pension plans and the insurance board) because they send the same objects; the other public body type covers prospects and the clients that joined after 2023.
The board of directors is treated as an external party so that board decisions can link to the processes they trigger.
cases_per_month for annual and quarterly processes is the average per month (for example 5 quarterly reports a quarter gives 1.67 a month).
Some web page titles in the source list are descriptive because the page heading was not captured; news release titles follow the release URL wording.
